_strings.@@6cfe5837a349: Treaty conformity — WV conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from WV income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the WV return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: WV's resident return (Form IT-140) starts from federal adjusted gross income (line 1). The 2025 instructions state plainly (p.24): "The starting point for the West Virginia income tax return is your federal adjusted gross income." Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from FAGI and flows through. WV's Schedule M "Modifications Increasing Federal Adjusted Gross Income" (lines 51-58) lists ONLY: interest/dividends on federal obligations exempt from federal but not state tax; interest/dividends on non-WV state/local bonds; interest on money borrowed to buy WV-exempt bonds; 402(e) lump-sum distributions; "Other income deducted from federal adjusted gross income but subject to state tax" (example given is IRC Section 199 income); and savings-plan/ABLE/Jumpstart withdrawals. There is NO add-back for tax-treaty income, foreign/nonresident-alien treaty income, or income excluded under a US tax treaty. Therefore treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed by WV -> conforms = true.
_strings.@@6d9896330e09: Senior Citizen Tax Credit (SCTC) — Restricted to homeowners who participate in the county Homestead Exemption program (generally age 65+ or permanently/totally disabled), who owe and pay a Class II property tax liability on a homestead-exemption-eligible home (assessed value greater than $20,000 before the $20,000 homestead exemption), and whose federal AGI is less than 150% of the federal poverty guidelines. The WV Tax Division mails Form WV SCTC-A to program participants; the original SCTC-A must be filed (preparer-created substitutes are denied).

_strings.@@ab6ec6b14d82: Family Tax Credit (FTC) — Low-income WV resident individuals/families who file with at least one exemption. Filers with zero exemptions cannot claim it, and persons who pay the federal Alternative Minimum Tax are ineligible. Eligibility and credit percentage depend on family size (number of exemptions, boxes a+b+c) and Modified Federal AGI. Computed on Schedule FTC-1 and attached to the return; if filing married-filing-separately use Table 2.
_strings.@@b7b928148542: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): DISABLED VETERAN'S PROPERTY TAX CREDIT EXTENDED TO A WIDOWED SPOUSE — a widowed spouse may now claim the credit if the deceased disabled veteran claimed it in the prior year, as long as the widow(er) has not remarried and the qualifying property has not been reclassified or sold. A refundable credit, claimed on Form IT-140 line 21, box B. Resolve via: 2025 IT-140 booklet, Important Information for 2025 (p.15), Disabled Veterans Real Property Tax Credit (p.20), IT-140 line 21 instructions (p.25); TSD 455.
_strings.@@bf3edade7d26: Homestead Excess Property Tax Credit (HEPTC) — Low-income owners of an owner-occupied WV residence whose WV real property tax paid (less any Senior Citizen Tax Credit) exceeds 4% of gross household income. Low-income means federal AGI of 300% or less of the federal poverty guideline for the household size. Homestead Exemption program participation is NOT required. No credit if any owner of the homestead is not a low-income person. Filers who pay federal AMT are flagged/excluded. Schedule HEPTC-1 and the Class 2 property tax receipt must be filed.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form IT-140 line 8: 'Income Tax Due (Check One)' with method checkboxes 'Tax Table', 'Rate Schedule', 'Nonresident/Part-year resident calculation schedule'. Line 7 feeding it reads 'West Virginia Taxable Income (line 4 minus lines 5 & 6) IF LESS THAN ZERO, ENTER ZERO'. Instructions p.24: 'LINE 8 WEST VIRGINIA INCOME TAX - Check the appropriate box to indicate the method you used to calculate your tax.' Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): surviving_spouse ($2,000 — Exemptions box (d): 'A surviving spouse may claim an additional exemption for the two (2) taxable years following the year in which the spouse died, provided he/she has not remarried before the end of the taxable year' (instructions p.24). One more $2,000 exemption included in box (e). NOT applied by calc.state_tax (the engine applies only the personal/dependent keys) — claim it on the form, or reflect it by raising exemptions_count only if eligible.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: TY2025 verification (2026-08-04): West Virginia's trigger-based reduction DID reach TY2025 — the booklet prints 2.22/2.96/3.33/4.44/4.82% (2024 printed 2.36/3.15/3.54/4.72/5.12). All eight printed constants across both schedules were re-derived and equal EXACT cumulative marginal sums (222.00 = 2.22%x10,000; 666.00 = 222 + 2.96%x15,000; 1,165.50 = 666 + 3.33%x15,000; 2,053.50 = 1,165.50 + 4.44%x20,000; Schedule II mirrors at half boundaries), so there is no printed-constant divergence to disclose for either schedule. Base guidance: Supply Form IT-140 line 4, West Virginia Adjusted Gross Income = line 1 federal adjusted gross income ('Enter your federal adjusted gross income as shown on Federal Form 1040') plus line 2 additions to income (Schedule M line 59) minus line 3 subtractions from income (Schedule M line 50). If the filer has no Schedule M modifications, line 4 equals federal AGI. The op then subtracts the shipped $2,000-per-exemption amounts (standard_deduction is 0 — West Virginia has none) to reproduce line 7 West Virginia Taxable Income, assuming line 5 (Low-Income Earned Income Exclusion, only available when federal AGI is $10,000 or less / $5,000 MFS) is zero. Adjudication note (two-pass): standard_deduction is null — West Virginia allows neither a standard deduction nor itemized deductions on Form IT-140 (the only base reductions are the $2,000-per-exemption line 6 amounts, shipped as personal/dependent). Rate-schedule constants re-verified against the 2025 IT-140 booklet (222.00 / 666.00 / 1,165.50 / 2,053.50). THE 2025 RATE CUT (corrected 2026-09-28, Phase J JS2 — this note had quoted the 2023 statute and 2024's rates): the shipped rates (2.22%/2.96%/3.33%/4.44%/4.82%) are W. Va. Code §11-21-4i, 'Rate of tax — Taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2025' (2024 Second Special Session SB 2033), which 'shall apply for all taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2025, and shall be in lieu of the rates of tax specified in §11-21-4g of this code and as those rates were modified by the application of §11-21-4h of this code in 2024' (https://code.wvlegislature.gov/11-21-4I/, fetched 2026-09-28) — it supersedes the Tax Commissioner's August 2024 administrative notice under the §11-21-4h trigger. Do not use the 2023-2024 §11-21-4g rates (2.36%-5.12%). TWO RATE SCHEDULES: Rate Schedule I applies 'if you checked 1 (Single), 2 (Head of household), 3 (Married filing joint), or 5 (Widow[er] with dependent child)'; it is duplicated here for single, married_filing_jointly, and head_of_household. Rate Schedule II applies only to filing status 4 (Married filing separately); its bracket bounds ($5,000/$12,500/$20,000/$30,000) were copied directly from the published schedule, not derived. The printed constants ($236.00/$708.50/$1,239.50/$2,183.50 on Schedule I; $118.00/$354.25/$619.75/$1,091.75 on Schedule II) exactly equal the cumulative sums of the prior brackets — no rounding divergence. TAX TABLE MANDATE BELOW $100,000: Line 8 instructions (p.24) — 'If your filing status is single, head of household, widow(er) with a dependent child or married filing jointly and your taxable income is less than $100,000, apply the amount of taxable income shown on line 7 to the Tax Table on page 36 and enter your tax on this line'; the rate schedule is for taxable income over $100,000. The table (booklet pp.36–40, last row $99,950–100,000 = $4,230) is band-midpoint based, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands — the filed form must use the table. Married-filing-separately filers CANNOT use the table at any income: 'If your filing status is Married Filling Separately you MUST use RATE SCHEDULE II to compute your tax.' NO STANDARD OR ITEMIZED DEDUCTION: West Virginia allows neither a standard deduction nor federal itemized deductions on Form IT-140 — the only across-the-board deduction is the $2,000-per-exemption allowance ('You can deduct $2,000 for every exemption claimed in your exemption schedule', p.24). standard_deduction is shipped as 0 for every filing status so the engine subtracts exemptions only. ZERO-EXEMPTION $500 ALLOWANCE NOT MODELED: 'If you claimed zero exemptions, enter $500 on this line [line 6]' (box (e) = 0, e.g. a filer claimable as a dependent on another return). The engine with exemptions_count=0 subtracts $0, not $500, so it can overstate tax by up to about $26 (5.12% of $500) for such filers — use the form's line 6 in that case. LOW-INCOME EARNED INCOME EXCLUSION (LINE 5) NOT MODELED: filers with federal AGI of $10,000 or less ($5,000 or less MFS) who have earned income may exclude the smaller of federal AGI, earned income, or $10,000 ($5,000 MFS) on line 5 before line 7 (worksheet, booklet p.29). The engine assumes line 5 = 0; it only affects returns with federal AGI at or below $10,000/$5,000. SCHEDULE M MODIFICATIONS COME BEFORE THE SUPPLIED BASE: the senior-citizen modification (up to $8,000 of income per taxpayer age 65+ or permanently/totally disabled), the up-to-$8,000 surviving-spouse decreasing modification, Social Security benefit modification, and all other Schedule M items are line 2/line 3 adjustments taken BEFORE line 4 — the caller must supply line 4 WV AGI already reflecting them. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE: the engine maps QSS to married_filing_jointly. West Virginia's own filing status 5, 'Widow(er) with dependent child', uses the SAME Rate Schedule I as married filing jointly and the same $2,000 exemptions, so the mapping reproduces the correct tax. ROUNDING: the booklet requires whole dollars ('Round off amounts to WHOLE DOLLARS – NO CENTS', Tips on Filing a Paper Return, printed page 16 / PDF page 18) and both rate-schedule examples say 'Round to nearest whole dollar' — consistent with the engine's half-up rounding to whole dollars. LINE 7 FLOOR: 'IF LESS THAN ZERO, ENTER ZERO' matches the engine's max(0, base_after). CREDITS ARE NOT EXEMPTIONS AND ARE NOT MODELED: line 8 tax is reduced on line 9 by the Tax Credit Recap Schedule credits — notably the Family Tax Credit (Schedule FTC-1), which can reduce the line 8 tax by up to 100% for low-income families based on family size and Modified Federal AGI, plus the refundable Senior Citizen Tax Credit (line 18) and Homestead Excess Property Tax Credit (line 19). The engine computes line 8 only; actual line 10 liability may be lower. No county or municipal income tax is collected through Form IT-140 — the return computes only the West Virginia state personal income tax.
